text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd said on Tuesday that sales for rose 3.3 percent to A$522 million for the nine months endede September 30, 1996, compared with A$505.1 million in the same period a year earlier.
Santos said sales revenue in the third quarter rose 11.7 percent on the previous corresponding quarter to $186.6 million.
Sales volume increased 8.3 percent to 10.4 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe), while production rose 9.4 percent to 10.5 million boe.
Managing director Ross Adler said in a statement the increases reflected the first full quarter of ethane sales and the contribution from the acquisition of Parker & Parsley Australasia.

Santos said in its quarterly report that the appreciation of the Australian dollar had reduced some of the potential gain to sales revenue from higher crude oil and naptha prices and increased the impact on sales revenue of lower LPG prices.

"At the same time, the appreciation of the Australian dollar has enabled Santos to realise gains on US dollar denominated debt hedging US dollar revenues," it said. Gas production rose 15.4 percent, crude oil production fell 6.3 percent, naptha production rose 2.4 percent and LPG production grew 9.3 percent.
Exploration expenditure for the quarter was A$34.2 million, up 70.1 percent from the 1995 third quarter, Santos said.
Total spending on exploration and development was A$92.0 million, up 115.5 per cent from A$42.7 million.
